Step 1 · Listen and read: a Maslenitsa weekend

Listen first, then read. Answer the five questions.

A Maslenitsa weekend
Read the text (after listening)

Last year I spent Maslenitsa in a small town near Kazan, where my grandmother lives.

On Saturday we went to the central square, where a big festival was taking place. There were stalls with hot tea and pancakes with different fillings, and children were playing games and climbing a pole to win a prize. In the evening, musicians in folk costumes sang old songs, and everybody joined in.

The best moment came on Sunday, the last day of the week. People gathered around a huge straw figure and burned it to say goodbye to winter. My grandmother says that after that day spring really begins. I took photographs all day and promised myself to come back next year.

In my opinion, such traditions are important because they remind us of our history and help neighbours get to know each other.

Текст авторский (на проверку); озвучка синтезатором речи.

1. Where did the narrator spend Maslenitsa?

The first sentence: “in a small town near Kazan, where my grandmother lives.”

2. What could people buy on the square?

“stalls with hot tea and pancakes with different fillings”

3. What did the children do?

“children were playing games and climbing a pole to win a prize”

4. What happened on the last day of the week?

“People gathered around a huge straw figure and burned it…”

5. Why does the narrator think such traditions are important?

The last sentence of the text.
